Create Candidate Stratification Variables

Source: R/strata_functions.R
create_stratification_candidates.Rd

Generates a set of candidate stratification variables for use in stratified model-assisted estimation. Creates single-variable stratifications (tertiles, quartiles, quintiles) for each specified variable, as well as interaction stratifications for all pairs of variables.

create_stratification_candidates(
  dat,
  vars,
  Z = NULL,
  jitter_vars = NULL,
  sd_jitter = 0.001,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

dat

Data frame containing the variables to stratify on.

vars

Character vector specifying the names of columns in dat to use for creating stratifications.

Z

Optional character string specifying the name of the treatment indicator variable in dat. If provided, stratifications are computed separately within each treatment arm, ensuring balanced strata across arms. Default is NULL (pooled stratification).

jitter_vars

Character vector specifying which variables (subset of vars) should have small random noise added before computing quantile breaks. This helps avoid ties that can cause cut() to fail. Default is NULL (no jitter applied).

sd_jitter

Numeric value specifying the standard deviation of the jitter noise. Default is 1e-3.

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducibility when jitter is applied. Default is NULL.

Value

A named list of factor vectors, each representing a candidate stratification. Names follow the convention:

Single-variable

{var}_tertiles, {var}_quartiles, {var}_quintiles

Interactions

{var1}_{var2}_2x2, {var1}_{var2}_2x3, {var1}_{var2}_3x2, {var1}_{var2}_3x3

Factor levels have meaningful labels (e.g., "Low Yhat", "Med Yhat / High word_count"). Stratifications that fail due to non-unique quantile breaks are automatically excluded from the output.

Details

For each variable in vars, the function creates three stratifications based on quantiles:

  • Tertiles (3 groups): Low, Med, High

  • Quartiles (4 groups): Low, Med-Low, Med-High, High

  • Quintiles (5 groups): Very Low, Low, Med, High, Very High

For each unique pair of variables, the function creates four interaction stratifications by crossing quantile groups:

  • 2x2: median split on both variables (4 strata)

  • 2x3: median split on first, tertiles on second (6 strata)

  • 3x2: tertiles on first, median split on second (6 strata)

  • 3x3: tertiles on both variables (9 strata)

When Z is provided, quantile breaks are computed separately within each treatment arm. This ensures that the same proportion of treated and control units fall into each stratum level, which is important for maintaining balance in stratified estimation.

When a variable has many tied values, quantile breaks may not be unique, causing cut() to fail. Use jitter_vars to add small random noise (SD = 0.001) to such variables before computing breaks.
